capabilities.target: private repositories owned by the user
public repository (pull request visible to anyone, including the issue author)

inputs.source: User's direct chat instruction to the desktop agent
Issue opened in the public GitHub repository, authored by any GitHub user
Tool definitions and behavior served by the unpinned github-mcp-server docker image

controls.name: Per-tool-call approval prompt with collapsed arguments
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees a collapsed, client-rendered summary rather than the raw destination and payload, and approves many calls per session, so a more persuasive model and higher call volume (approval fatigue, SAFE-T1403) degrade its effectiveness (ASI09).

controls.name: Repo-scoped fine-grained PAT excluding private repos
controls.decay_rationale: A token scoped only to the public repository makes the private repository unreadable by this agent regardless of injected instructions or model capability.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review (full arguments shown)
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the actual file paths/contents and PR diff, instead of a model-written summary, removes the model's ability to understate cross-repo data movement.

controls.name: Structural block on read-private-then-write-public in one session
controls.decay_rationale: A policy enforced outside the model that refuses to let a single session both read a private repo and write to a public repo blocks the exfiltration chain structurally, independent of approval behavior.

controls.name: Pinned or hashed github-mcp-server image
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning the image digest and verifying its signature prevents silent tool redefinition (rug pull) from an upstream image update.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta via indirect issue injection defeats collapsed-summary approval gate (TC1 + TC9)

attack_path.note: Attacker opens an issue in the public repo containing hidden instructions telling the agent to read private repository contents and open a pull request containing them.
The agent's single GitHub PAT carries repo scope across every repository the user owns, so it can read private repo files on the injected instruction's behalf.
The agent opens a pull request on the public repo containing the private data, making it visible to anyone, including the issue's author.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

findings.residual_rationale: The mechanical step-2 approval-gate credit floors residual at moderate, but this exact design (collapsed-argument, high-volume per-call approval on one shared broad-scope token) is the publicly documented GitHub MCP server exfiltration pattern: approvers could not see that a file-read call and a PR-create call together moved private data into a public PR. The gate is treated as already weakened today rather than only under a future trigger, so residual is rated high rather than the computed moderate floor.

forecast.watch_signal: The approval UI switches to 'always allow' for this server or session, the per-call prompt is removed or auto-approved, or the underlying model is upgraded to one that writes more convincing per-call summaries.

evidence.observation: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN is passed to a single shared github MCP server process; no per-repository or per-visibility scoping is configured.
The personal access token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, so any tool call through this server can read private repos.
Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, making issue bodies an untrusted (U) input that enters the agent's context when it is asked to review open issues.
The client approval prompt collapses arguments by default and users approve many calls per session: a model_summary review mode subject to approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

The user's own instruction only asks the agent to look at public issues; the in.public_issue content is the vector that must redirect the agent toward the private-repo-to-public-PR path, matching the publicly reported GitHub MCP server exfiltration vulnerability.

recommendations.action: Issue a fine-grained PAT scoped only to the public repository for this agent, or use separate tokens/sessions for public vs private repo access so no single session holds both.
Change the approval UI to show the raw action (full file paths/contents read and full PR diff) instead of a collapsed model-generated summary before approval.
Add a structural rule that blocks any single session from both reading a private repository and writing to a public repository.

findings.title: Unpinned github-mcp-server image allows silent tool redefinition reaching the same exfiltration sink (ASI04)

attack_path.note: Docker image is pulled by name with no tag or digest pin (definitions_pinned: false), so an upstream or registry compromise changes behavior silently.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: Same approval-gate removal/weakening signals as the main finding; additionally, a change in the pulled image digest or tag without a corresponding review.

evidence.observation: The docker run command references ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no image tag or digest, resolving to whatever 'latest' currently publishes.

The same broad-scope PAT is available to whatever tool definitions the image currently serves, so a compromised image version could redefine get_file_contents or create_pull_request to add hidden exfiltration behavior without any config change on the user's side.

recommendations.action: Pin the github-mcp-server image to an immutable digest and verify its signature before each pull.
Log and diff the MCP server's tools/list response between sessions to detect silent tool redefinition.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted public-issue input can reach a broad-scope, cross-repository credential and an irreversible public-egress action (create_pull_request), the classic lethal trifecta. The only control in place, a per-call approval prompt, shows collapsed/summarized arguments and is approved at high volume per session, which is documented (approval fatigue, ASI09, SAFE-T1403) to fail against exactly this pattern; residual is therefore rated high rather than the mechanical moderate floor the step-2 approval-gate credit would otherwise allow. Forecast risk is critical: model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal each independently defeat this model-summary approval gate (control_decay.md), and no structural control (scoped token, raw-action review, or a cross-repo block) is currently in place to take over. The single highest-leverage fix is scoping the PAT so it cannot read private repositories at all, which would sever the path and drop residual to low regardless of model capability or approval behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (mcp config, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No system prompt or agent instructions artifact was supplied, so the instructions review (ambiguous_goal, unbounded_scope, and related issue types) could not be performed; this may understate goal-hijack risk.

The full github-mcp-server tool catalog was not provided; only get_file_contents (private repos) and create_pull_request (public repo) were named as stable ids, so other tools exposed by the server (issue comments, code search, webhook management, etc.) are not inventoried and could add further egress or write paths.

Confidence in the approval gate's exact behavior (model_summary review mode) is based on the runtime note's description of collapsed arguments rather than direct inspection of the client's approval UI implementation.
